entry.title: How to get and use Contribution Points in Crimson Desert
entry.summary:
Crimson Desert has different factions to interest you in different tasks, and completing those will help you get Contribution Points. Different from your staple currency, Contribution Points can be used to get different items in the game.
While you'll have a limited amount of Contribution Points to begin with, you'll be able to get more from in-game activities.
Table of contents How to get Contribution Points in Crimson Desert How to use Contribution Points in Crimson Desert
How to get Contribution Points in Crimson Desert
Contribution Points in Crimson Desert are essentially faction points that you get from completing various faction quests. Every faction has specific tasks and requests you get to complete. These are largely optional content that's different from the main quests. However, finishing these tasks can be immensely rewarding to level yourself up.
Image via Pearl Abyss
Open your Journal tab, and then select the Faction Quests to view all the available tasks. These tasks will mostly be from one of the following options.
Defeat bandits
Help beggars
Liberate areas
Bounties
Some main story quests.
How to use Contribution Points in Crimson Desert
Image via Pearl Abyss
Once you've enough Contribution Points, you can use the currency at Contribution Shops. There are separate shops for every faction in Crimson Desert. The items you get from the shops also vary based on the faction.
When you're in Hernand, take the path that leads you to the castle. You'll find a door on the main path (towards the castle). Head inside, and you'll find Haldwin. You can then choose to spend your Contribution Points to buy whatever you want and need.

entry.title: How to complete Salvatore bounty in Crimson Desert and catch him
entry.summary:
The Salvatore bounty is one of the latter set of contracts in Crimson Desert, and you'll need to capture the outlaw to bring him to justice. However, the job is easier said than done, as you'll need to find him from his hideout. That comes after you accept the poster that states the details of the bounty on offer.
This guide will help you to complete the bounty that involves tracking down and catching Salvatore.
Table of contents How to start Salvatore bounty in Crimson Desert How to catch Salvatore in Crimson Desert
How to start Salvatore bounty in Crimson Desert
Like all bounties, the one for Salvatore can be found in Hernand City. You can look for such lamp posts all around Hernand City. You can also find the bounty on the notice board in the city. The notice board will be highlighted with a purple icon on the map.
Image via Pearl Abyss
Once you find the poster, it will provide you with all the necessary information for finding Salvatore. His hideout is located in the southernmost part of Hernand near the Sunset Valley. Once you head to Sunset Valley, go to the back of the town. Here, you'll find the windmill.
Screenshot and remix by Destructoid
You can enter the windmill using the main door, and Salvatore can be found there.
How to catch Salvatore in Crimson Desert
Image via Pearl Abyss
Once you enter the windmill, you'll find Salvatore over there. He will try to flee upon seeing you. Get close to tackle him down, and tie him up. Then, pick and carry him to the nearest constabulary in Hernand. Make sure to deliver him alive, as that will increase the total rewards that you receive.
When you complete this bounty, you'll get 12 Silver as your reward (reduced if he dies in the process).

A man who alleges he is a programmer at Roblox has been arrested in New Orleans after being charged with child pornography possession as well as possession of a child sex doll. According to WBRZ2, Roblox Corporation dismissed Borne's claims, saying he "has never worked for the company."
"The individual is not, and has never been, a Roblox employee," the company told that news channel.
This arrest comes months after Louisiana AG Liz Murril filed a lawsuit against Roblox Corporation, alleging it "has permitted and perpetuated an online environment in which child predators thrive, directly contributing to the widespread victimization of minor children in Louisiana."
Roblox has been the target of several similar lawsuits over the last few months, such as the one from LA County, itself alleging that children in its jurisdiction "have been repeatedly exposed to sexually explicit content, exploitation, and grooming on Roblox."

The Warren bounty is one of the more advanced contracts you can complete in Crimson Desert, but to do so, you'll have to figure out where the outlaw is hiding. Once you find him, you'll then need to capture and hand him over to jail.

To begin the Warren Bounty, you'll need to view the poster from a lamp post. These lamp posts don't have fixed locations, but you can find them all around Hernand. You can also find the poster on the notice board in Hernand City.

Once you find the notice board, you'll find all the relevant details of the bounty on the poster. The details include the last-seen location of Warren, and you have to trace him from there. Instead, you need to complete The Unreachable Village quest. You'll need to interact with Arkin and Shai. Then, you have to retrieve the Relic of Pororin and deliver it back to Arkin. This will allow you to access the Pororin Forest area.

entry.title: How to complete Alessio Bounty in Crimson Desert and capture him
entry.summary:
There are several bounties to complete in the Hernand region in Crimson Desert, and one of them involves taking down Alessio. Doing so gets you different rewards, but the payout depends on whether Alessio is returned alive or not.
Compared to some of the previous bounties, Alessio's quest is slightly trickier. However, the basic structure is the same as the other ones: you locate the bounty target from its hideout, capture it, and then bring it to jail.
Table of contents How to start the Alessio Bounty in Crimson Desert How to capture Alessio in Crimson Desert
How to start the Alessio Bounty in Crimson Desert
You can find Alessio's bounty post on random lamp poles across Hernand. The exact location will be random based on your save. You can also find it on the notice board in Hernand, which is highlighted in purple on the map. Open the bounty post to accept the contract, and it will also reveal where Alessio was last seen in the open.
Image via Pearl Abyss
To track down Alessio, you'll need to travel to the southeast of Hernand. The hideout is near the Trembling Gorge, and you can reach it using the road that goes north into Ironwood. You can travel on foot, but riding a horse is better (keeping the distance in mind).
How to capture Alessio in Crimson Desert
Screenshot and remix by Destructoid
Once you reach the location marked on the image above, you'll find Alessio along with his henchmen. It's easy to identify Alessio as he is highlighted on the map. Additionally, he limps when he walks, which is the easiest visual cue.
Image via Pearl Abyss
First, you should take down the other enemies. While you do so, try not to assassinate Alessio since that will reduce the final payout. Once you capture Alessio, drop him off at the nearest constabulary, and you'll get all your rewards.

entry.title: How to complete Destroy Exospire in Helldivers 2
entry.summary:
March 20 has activated the Destroy Exospire mission in Helldivers 2, and it involves taking down the storm formations on planet Seasse. However, the job is easier said than done, and you can expect plenty of enemies that will try to disrupt your attempt. Let's look at how to easily complete the new quest that arrives as part of the Machinery of Oppression update.
Helldivers 2 Destroy Exospire walkthrough
Image via Arrowhead
Once you accept the quest from the terminal, head to Seasse to begin the quest. The Exospire is a massive-purple colored structure that is almost impossible to miss. When you reach its base, you'll realize that a giant shield blocks the entrance. You have to take this shield down before you can proceed further.
Image via Arrowhead
First, look for the sub-objective that requires you to disrupt a Shield Generator. You'll find the generator close to the Exospire. Keep shooting at the generator's shield until it gets destroyed. Next, destroy the generator by calling the Data Jack stratagem. Once the stratagem becomes active, enemies will start spawning on you.
Image via Arrowhead
To complete the process, you'll need to clear all enemies. Finally, initiate the power surge to bring down the shield that restricts you from entering the base of the Exospire. Once inside, you'll have to destroy 148 Dark Fluid Cells. These cells are on the walls, and you can start to shoot at them. However, you'll also have to be mindful of enemies who will try to stop you from succeeding.
The core will become completely destabilized when all the Dark Fluid Cells are destroyed. The core will then explode, and your task will be complete. When the core explodes, try to run as far away as possible. Otherwise, you'll get eliminated by the explosion (the task will still be completed irrespective of the results).

entry.title: USN-8103-2: Exiv2 regression
entry.summary:
USN-8103-1 fixed vulnerabilities in Exiv2. The update caused a regression for Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu 25.10. This update fixes the problem.
We apologize for the inconvenience.
Original advisory details:
It was discovered that Exiv2 did not correctly handle reading certain buffers. An attacker could possibly use this issue to leak sensitive information. This issue only affected Ubuntu 16.04 LTS and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2020-18771)
Wen Cheng discovered that Exiv2 did not correctly handle certain memory allocation. If a user or system were tricked into opening a specially crafted file, an attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 16.04 LTS and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2020-18899)
It was discovered that Exiv2 did not correctly handle writing certain metadata. If a user or system were tricked into opening a specially crafted file, an attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2025-54080)
It was discovered that Exiv2 did not correctly handle parsing certain metadata. If a user or system were tricked into opening a specially crafted file, an attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu 25.10. (CVE-2025-55304)
It was discovered that Exiv2 did not correctly handle parsing certain images. If a user or system were tricked into opening a specially crafted file, an attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2026-25884)
It was discovered that Exiv2 did not correctly handle previewing certain images. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2026-27596)
It was discovered that Exiv2 did not correctly handle certain integer arithmetic. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2026-27631)

entry.title: USN-8018-3: Python 2.7 vulnerabilities
entry.summary:
USN-8018-1 fixed CVE-2025-12084, CVE-2025-15282, CVE-2026-0672, CVE-2026-0865 for python3. This update provides the corresponding updates for python2.7.
Original advisory details:
Denis Ledoux discovered that Python incorrectly parsed email message headers. An attacker could possibly use this issue to inject arbitrary headers into email messages. This issue only affected python3.6, python3.7, python3.8, python3.9, python3.10, python3.11, python3.12, python3.13, and python3.14 packages. (CVE-2025-11468)
Jacob Walls, Shai Berger, and Natalia Bidart discovered that Python inefficiently parsed XML input with quadratic complexity. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2025-12084)
It was discovered that Python incorrectly parsed malicious plist files. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Python to use excessive resources, leading to a denial of service. This issue only affected python3.5, python3.6, python3.7, python3.8, python3.9, python3.10, python3.11, python3.12, python3.13, and python3.14 packages. (CVE-2025-13837)
Omar Hasan discovered that Python incorrectly parsed URL mediatypes. An attacker could possibly use this issue to inject arbitrary HTTP headers. (CVE-2025-15282)
Omar Hasan discovered that Python incorrectly parsed malicious IMAP inputs. An attacker could possibly use this issue to inject arbitrary IMAP commands. (CVE-2025-15366)
Omar Hasan discovered that Python incorrectly parsed malicious POP3 inputs. An attacker could possibly use this issue to inject arbitrary POP3 commands. (CVE-2025-15367)
Omar Hasan discovered that Python incorrectly parsed malicious HTTP cookie headers. An attacker could possibly use this issue to inject arbitrary HTTP headers. (CVE-2026-0672)
Omar Hasan discovered that Python incorrectly parsed malicious HTTP header names and values. An attacker could possibly use this issue to inject arbitrary HTTP headers. (CVE-2026-0865)

entry.title: Far Cry's name is very ironic, if you're an armchair etymologist
entry.summary:
During a random dictionary delve last week I learned that "explore" once meant to cry out. It comes from an old Latin word formed from the prefix "ex-", describing outwardness, and "plorare", meaning to cry or weep. Compare "implore" - to beg, cry for something - and "deplore" - to berate, 'cry of' something or somebody.
The OED explains ("ex + "planō", meaning to level off, flatten for understanding) that "explore" may originally have referred to hunters, shouting to scare up animals lurking in the area around them. Exploration was always somewhat predatory, then, perhaps a little anguished. I have to admit, I got misty-eyed on discovering all this, thinking about how this word I've written a million times in videogame reviews is a kind of silenced wail.

The developers assembled at their San Francisco offices, some came from nearby, others from as far away as Vancouver, Canada and Winchester in the UK.
